correctness.rationale: For p>5, translation by -a/5 preserves the coefficient average and reduces to x^5+Bx^3+ux^2+vx, B=b-2a^2/5. Fiber inclusion-exclusion is exact for degree 5. For r=1,2,3 the numbers of free coefficient pairs are q^2,q,1. Four- and five-point constraints are respectively sum x_i^2+(sum x_i)^2=-2B and sum x_i=0 with sum x_i^2=-2B. Equality-partition Möbius inversion yields the explicit weight/determinant tables. All relevant forms are nondegenerate for p>5. Standard quadratic Gauss formulas give K4 and K5 in both t=0 and t!=0 cases. Symbolic simplification independently checks their substitution into the final exact rational identity. The gap is (q chi(5)-chi(-15))/(3q^2), nonzero for q>=7. Direct enumerations over prime fields and quadratic extensions, including original unnormalized coefficients and independent subset counts, passed. Finite checks are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The exact inclusion-exclusion identity and quadratic representation counts are explicitly known and not claimed new. The contribution is evaluation of the previously unevaluated K4 and K5 for the natural (d,s)=(5,2) family, leading to a closed exact character-stratified average for every p>5. Published papers I, II and III and Cohen contain estimates or uncomputed interpolating-set expressions, but their inspected principal theorems do not imply the displayed exact coefficients without new evaluation. value.rationale: For monic quintics the first two fixed coefficients form the natural (d,s)=(5,2) boundary just outside sharp previous exact-O(1) error estimate ranges. The computed invariant is the complete mean image-size law for all finite fields of characteristic p>5, not an arbitrary small-field slice. It resolves both last interpolation terms exactly and reveals three structural strata B=0, square and nonsquare, including a guaranteed nonzero class gap for every allowed q. This supplies usable exact arithmetic data not implied by broad first-moment bounds; no separate downstream theorem is claimed.
